track.name: startup-finance
track.label: Startup Finance & Unit Economics
track.summary: Master the financial language of startups — from burn rate and runway to CAC/LTV, fundraising term sheets, SaaS metrics, and cap table mechanics that founders and operators need to grow with confidence.

phases.title: Startup Accounting Basics
phases.description: Build the financial foundation every startup operator needs — understand the three core statements, accrual vs cash accounting, and the financial structure that supports growth.

phases.title: Unit Economics & CAC/LTV
phases.description: Learn to calculate customer acquisition cost and lifetime value, interpret the LTV:CAC ratio, and use unit economics to decide when a business model is actually working.

phases.title: Runway & Cash Management
phases.description: Track burn rate, extend runway, manage working capital, and build the cash flow models that keep a startup solvent through the gaps between funding rounds.

phases.title: Fundraising Mechanics & Term Sheets
phases.description: Understand the funding stages from pre-seed to Series A, decode a term sheet, and evaluate SAFEs and convertible notes before signing anything.

phases.title: SaaS Metrics & Revenue Models
phases.description: Master the SaaS metrics dashboard — ARR, MRR, churn, net revenue retention, and the benchmarks investors use to evaluate recurring revenue businesses.

phases.title: Cap Table & Equity Compensation
phases.description: Model a cap table through multiple funding rounds, understand dilution and the option pool shuffle, and design employee stock option plans that attract top talent.

topics.title: Startup Accounting Fundamentals
topics.description: Learn how accrual accounting differs from cash accounting, why startups use both, and what your accountant actually does each month.

topics.title: P&L, Balance Sheet & Cash Flow
topics.description: Read the three core financial statements as an operator — understand what each one tells you about the health and trajectory of your business.

topics.title: Financial Structure for Startups
topics.description: Set up a chart of accounts, choose the right entity type, and understand the financial infrastructure that makes reporting and fundraising easier.

topics.title: Calculating CAC and LTV
topics.description: Compute blended and channel-level customer acquisition cost and lifetime value — and understand why the ratio between them determines business model viability.

topics.title: CAC Payback Period
topics.description: Calculate how many months of gross margin it takes to recover what you spent to acquire a customer — a key signal for capital efficiency and growth sustainability.

topics.title: Unit Economics for Non-SaaS Models
topics.description: Adapt the CAC/LTV framework to marketplace, e-commerce, and transactional models where contribution margin per order replaces monthly recurring revenue.

topics.title: Burn Rate & Runway
topics.description: Calculate gross and net burn rate, forecast your runway at the current spend trajectory, and identify the levers that extend it without killing growth.

topics.title: Cash Flow Forecasting
topics.description: Build a 13-week cash forecast that tracks inflows and outflows at the transaction level — the model investors ask for when a startup is approaching the end of its runway.

topics.title: Working Capital & Cash Efficiency
topics.description: Manage accounts receivable, payable, and inventory cycles to optimise cash timing — understand why profitable companies still run out of cash.

topics.title: Startup Funding Stages
topics.description: Map the fundraising journey from angels and pre-seed through Series A, B, and C — understand what investors at each stage expect to see in traction and metrics.

topics.title: Term Sheet Basics
topics.description: Decode the key provisions of a VC term sheet — valuation, liquidation preferences, pro-rata rights, anti-dilution clauses, and board composition.

topics.title: SAFEs & Convertible Notes
topics.description: Understand the mechanics of the Y Combinator SAFE and the convertible note — valuation caps, discount rates, and how they convert to equity at the next priced round.

topics.title: ARR, MRR & Churn
topics.description: Build ARR and MRR waterfalls showing new, expansion, contraction, and churn — the four components investors use to diagnose the health of a SaaS business.

topics.title: Net Revenue Retention & Expansion
topics.description: Calculate net and gross revenue retention, understand why NRR above 100% creates compounding growth, and benchmark cohort retention against industry standards.

topics.title: The SaaS Metrics Dashboard
topics.description: Assemble the metrics every SaaS board deck needs — ARR growth, NRR, LTV:CAC, payback period, Rule of 40, and magic number.

topics.title: Cap Table Structure
topics.description: Build a cap table from incorporation through multiple rounds — model how each new investment changes ownership percentages across founders, employees, and investors.

topics.title: Employee Stock Options (ESOPs)
topics.description: Understand how option grants work — strike price, vesting schedules, cliff periods, exercise windows, and how to communicate equity value to candidates.

topics.title: Dilution & Option Pool Shuffle
topics.description: Model dilution through new investment rounds, understand the option pool shuffle, and evaluate how liquidation preferences affect founder outcomes at exit.

resources.title: Startup Accounting Guide — Stripe Atlas
resources.note: Stripe Atlas's plain-English guide to startup accounting — explains accrual vs cash basis, what monthly close looks like, and what to expect from your bookkeeper.

resources.title: Accounting Resources — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: CFI's full accounting resource library — covers the concepts a startup operator needs: revenue recognition, accruals, and the language accountants use every month.

resources.title: Three Financial Statements — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Explains how the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement connect to each other — the linkage that every operator needs to understand before reading their monthly accounts.

resources.title: Balance Sheet — Investopedia
resources.note: Clear, jargon-free overview of balance sheet structure — assets, liabilities, and equity — with worked examples and what each section signals about financial health.

resources.title: Stripe Atlas Guides — Startup Finance & Legal
resources.note: Stripe Atlas's full library of startup guides — covers entity formation, banking, accounting, and the financial infrastructure decisions founders make at incorporation.

resources.title: Chart of Accounts — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Explains how a chart of accounts is structured — numbering conventions, account types, and how to set up categories that make fundraising diligence straightforward.

resources.title: SaaS Metrics 2.0 — For Entrepreneurs
resources.note: David Skok's definitive guide to SaaS unit economics — the most-shared resource on CAC and LTV for startup founders, packed with worked examples and benchmarks.

resources.title: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Explains how to calculate LTV with multiple methods — simple, historical, and predictive — and how to use it alongside CAC to evaluate channel profitability.

resources.title: The SaaS CFO — CAC Payback Period Guide
resources.note: Ben Murray's step-by-step walkthrough of the CAC payback calculation — gross margin adjusted vs unadjusted versions, and what payback benchmarks look like across SaaS stages.

resources.title: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) — Investopedia
resources.note: Clean formula-based explanation of CAC — what to include in the numerator, how to segment by channel, and why the number changes as you scale your sales team.

resources.title: Unit Economics — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains unit economics for non-SaaS models — contribution margin per unit, how to calculate breakeven, and what investors look for in marketplace and e-commerce businesses.

resources.title: Gross Margin — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Covers gross margin calculation across different business models — essential for adapting unit economics to non-subscription revenue streams like services or physical goods.

resources.title: Burn Rate — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains gross vs net burn rate with formulas, shows how to calculate months of runway, and describes the warning signs that a startup needs to reduce spend or raise faster.

resources.title: YC Library — Startup Finance Topics
resources.note: Y Combinator's free library of essays and videos from Startup School — the finance and fundraising section covers burn, runway, and default alive vs default dead.

resources.title: Cash Flow Forecast — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Step-by-step guide to building a cash flow forecast — explains the 13-week model format, rolling vs static approaches, and how to present the output to a board.

resources.title: Startup Financial Models Guide — Stripe Atlas
resources.note: Stripe Atlas's guide to building your first financial model — covers revenue and expense assumptions, cash flow projections, and how to make a model useful for decision-making rather than just fundraising.

resources.title: Working Capital — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains working capital — the difference between current assets and liabilities — and why managing AR, AP, and inventory cycles can make or break a company's cash position.

resources.title: Cash Conversion Cycle — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Covers the cash conversion cycle formula — days inventory + days receivable minus days payable — and how shortening it frees up cash without cutting headcount.

resources.title: Startup Funding Stages — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains the full funding journey from seed to Series C — what each stage is designed to fund, what metrics investors expect, and the typical dilution at each step.

resources.title: Startup Funding Guide — Carta Blog
resources.note: Carta's practical overview of startup funding rounds — covers pre-seed through Series A, typical round sizes, and the cap table implications of each stage.

resources.title: Term Sheet — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains every major clause in a VC term sheet — valuation, liquidation preference, anti-dilution provisions, and drag-along rights — with definitions written for first-time founders.

resources.title: Venture Capital Term Sheet — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: CFI's guide to term sheet provisions — explains how each clause shifts risk and reward between founders and investors, with example negotiation scenarios.

resources.title: Y Combinator SAFE Documents
resources.note: The official YC SAFE documents — post-money and pre-money versions with explanatory notes — the standard instrument for early-stage fundraising used across thousands of startups.

resources.title: Convertible Note — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains the convertible note mechanics — principal, interest rate, maturity, valuation cap, and discount — and compares them to SAFEs for early-stage fundraising.

resources.title: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Explains ARR and MRR calculation, how to build the ARR waterfall (new, expansion, contraction, churn), and why investors focus on net new ARR as the primary growth signal.

resources.title: The SaaS CFO — SaaS Metrics Guide
resources.note: Ben Murray's comprehensive guide to SaaS metrics — definitions, formulas, and benchmarks for ARR, MRR, churn, and every metric a SaaS CFO tracks monthly.

resources.title: Why Churn Is So Critical to SaaS Success — For Entrepreneurs
resources.note: David Skok's analysis of how even small churn rates destroy long-term value — the maths of why net revenue retention above 100% is the most important SaaS metric.

resources.title: Net Revenue Retention — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Explains the difference between gross and net revenue retention, how to calculate them from cohort data, and what NRR benchmarks look like at Seed vs Series A vs growth stage.

resources.title: SaaS Metrics — For Entrepreneurs
resources.note: David Skok's original SaaS metrics post — the complete dashboard of metrics from MRR to CAC to churn that every SaaS board deck is built on.

resources.title: 16 Startup Metrics — a16z
resources.note: Andreessen Horowitz's canonical list of the sixteen metrics VCs use to evaluate startups — definitions, formulas, and why each one matters for Series A readiness.

resources.title: Capitalization Table — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains cap table structure — how to read it, what fully diluted shares means, and how ownership percentages change through each funding round.

resources.title: Cap Table Guide — Carta Blog
resources.note: Carta's practical guide to building and maintaining a cap table — covers round modelling, how to add new investors, and when a spreadsheet stops working and you need dedicated software.

resources.title: Stock Options — Investopedia
resources.note: Covers how stock options work — the difference between ISOs and NSOs, how vesting schedules and cliffs work, and the tax implications for employees at exercise and sale.

resources.title: Equity 101: Stock Options — Carta Blog
resources.note: Carta's equity explainer for employees and founders — explains strike prices, vesting, exercise windows, and how to communicate option value honestly to candidates.

resources.title: Dilution — Investopedia
resources.note: Explains stock dilution in detail — how new share issuances reduce existing ownership, how to calculate post-round ownership, and when dilution is good (if growth justifies it).

resources.title: Liquidation Preference — Corporate Finance Institute
resources.note: Explains liquidation preference mechanics — 1x non-participating vs participating preferred — and models how different structures affect founder and employee payouts at various exit valuations.
